newsitem.title: USA: IMF warns of possible risks to Thai banking system.
newsitem.headline: IMF warns of possible risks to Thai banking system.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund warned Thailand on Wednesday of potential risks to its banking system.

"The ability of the banking system to withstand a more turbulent domestic or foreign environment -- including reduced access to foreign markets, a sustained increase in domestic interest rates, and lower growth rates -- cannot be taken for granted," IMF staff said in a report on world capital markets.
The report pointed to "negative indicators" in the recent performance of the Thai banking industry, particularly a decline in liquidity and expansion of foreign liabilities.
"The situation for Thai banks is likely to become more difficult in the future," it added.
The banks are facing increasing competition from other financial institutions as the barriers between market sectors weaken, according to the report.
Samll banks, which have seen the fastest loan expansion and a narrowing of interest margins in recent years, are likely to be hurt the most, it added.
"According to standard indicators, the banking system in Thailand appears robust," the IMF report said.
But lending has grown rapidly over the past five years and is highly concentrated in a few large industrial conglomerates and real estate borrowers, it said.
Banks have also used short-term domestic and foreign liabilities to finance a substantial amount of medium- and long-term loans, it added.
